blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 324 of the Indian Constitution provides the legal foundation for the Election Commission of India.
The ECI is a multi-member body comprising the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners appointed by the President.
The CEC enjoys security of tenure and can only be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge.
The Commission possesses administrative, advisory, and quasi-judicial powers regarding electoral operations and disputes.
ECI enforces the Model Code of Conduct (MCC), prepares electoral rolls, and accords recognition to political parties and symbols.

blocks.content: The Election Commission of India (ECI) is one of the most important constitutional bodies in India.
It is responsible for conducting free, fair, impartial and transparent elections in the country.
The success of Indian democracy largely depends upon the independent functioning of the Election Commission.
It ensures that political power is transferred peacefully and democratically.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar regarded free and fair elections as the backbone of democracy.
The Election Commission is established under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution. Article 324 provides:

items:
• Superintendence of elections
  • Direction and control of elections
  • Conduct of elections to:
    • Parliament
    • State Legislatures
    • Office of President
    • Office of Vice-President

Conduct of elections to:
  • Parliament
  • State Legislatures
  • Office of President
  • Office of Vice-President

blocks.content: Thus, ECI is a constitutional authority, not a statutory body.
Originally, the Election Commission was a single-member body. In 1989, it became a multi-member body.
All three have equal powers and take decisions by majority.

blocks.content: Powers of Election Commission can be classified into:

items:
• Preparation and revision of electoral rolls
  • Registration of voters
  • Conduct of elections
  • Announcement of election schedule
  • Appointment of election officials
  • Supervision of polling and counting
  • Allotment of election symbols
  • Recognition of political parties
Preparation and revision of electoral rolls

blocks.content: The Election Commission gives advice to:

items:
• President regarding disqualification of MPs
  • Governor regarding disqualification of MLAs Its advice is binding in such matters.
Governor regarding disqualification of MLAs Its advice is binding in such matters.

blocks.content: The Commission acts as a quasi-judicial body in:

items:
• Disputes regarding recognition of political parties
  • Disputes related to election symbols
  • Disqualification of members
Disputes regarding recognition of political parties

blocks.content: It can issue orders similar to courts.

blocks.content: Model Code of Conduct is a set of guidelines issued by ECI. Purpose:

items:
• Ensure free and fair elections
  • Prevent misuse of official machinery
  • Maintain political neutrality

blocks.content: It becomes operational from the date of election announcement till declaration of result.
Electoral roll is a list of eligible voters. Eligibility:

items:
• Citizen of India
  • 18 years of age
  • Ordinary resident of constituency

blocks.content: Election symbols help illiterate voters identify candidates. Symbol allotment is done by ECI.

ECI conducts elections for Parliament, State Legislatures, President, and Vice-President, but NOT for local municipal/panchayat bodies (which are conducted by State Election Commissions).
The CEC and other Election Commissioners have equal powers and draw the same salary and allowances as a judge of the Supreme Court.
While the CEC can be removed only via parliamentary address, other Election Commissioners are removed by the President on the recommendation of the CEC.

blocks.content: The Election Commission of India is the guardian of democracy.
Its independence, integrity and efficiency determine the quality of elections in India. A strong Election Commission ensures a strong democracy.
